title_en: Foshan Municipal People's Government v. Bank of Communications, Hong Kong Branch — guarantee dispute
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 3 of the Guarantee Law, guarantee activities shall follow the principles of equality, voluntariness, fairness, and good faith. If a third party unrelated to the loan contract issues a letter of undertaking to the contract creditor but does not explicitly express an intention to assume suretyship liability or repay on behalf of the debtor, it cannot be presumed that the act of issuing the letter of undertaking constitutes a suretyship within the meaning of the Guarantee Law.

Foshan Municipal People's Government v. Bank of Communications Co., Ltd., Hong Kong Branch — Dispute over Guarantee

[Foshan Municipal People's Government v. Bank of Communications Co., Ltd., Hong Kong Branch — Dispute over Guarantee]

Ruling Summary

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 3 of the Guarantee Law, guarantee activities shall follow the principles of equality, voluntariness, fairness, and good faith. Where a third party unrelated to the loan contract issues a letter of undertaking (commitment letter) to the creditor of the contract, but does not explicitly express an assumption of suretyship liability or repayment on behalf of the debtor, such act of issuing the letter of undertaking shall not be presumed to constitute a suretyship within the meaning of the Guarantee Law.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 5

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Foshan Municipal People's Government. Domicile: No. 14 Dafu Road, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Liang Shaotang, Mayor of the city.

Agent ad litem: Guo Zhongcheng, lawyer of Beijing Tonghezheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Shan Sujian, lawyer of Guangdong Tianlun Law Firm, Foshan Branch.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Bank of Communications Co., Ltd., Hong Kong Branch. Domicile: 20 Pedder Street, Central, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Representative: Chen Xiafang, Deputy General Manager of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Shen Zhigeng, lawyer of Beijing Zongheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Wenyue, Assistant Business Manager of the Branch.

The appellant, Foshan Municipal People's Government (hereinafter referred to as Foshan Municipal Government), filed an appeal with this Court against the civil judgment (2001) Yue Fa Jing Er Chu Zi No. 1 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) in the case of its dispute over guarantee with the respondent, Bank of Communications Co., Ltd., Hong Kong Branch (hereinafter referred to as Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Wang Yun serving as the presiding judge, and acting judges Chen Jizhong and Zhou Xiang participating in the deliberation, and heard this case. The trial has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

On May 8, 1994, Foshan Municipal Government issued a "Letter of Undertaking" numbered Fo Fu Han (1994) No. 030 to Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications, stating: "Zhongya Enterprises Limited (hereinafter referred to as Zhongya Company) is an institution of our city stationed in Hong Kong. In order to further develop the company's foreign trade business, the company hereby applies to your bank for a credit facility of USD 10 million. The above-mentioned application for a credit facility has been approved by our city government upon study. Please provide support to the company stationed in Hong Kong in accordance with its actual business development needs. This government is willing to urge the company stationed in Hong Kong to faithfully perform its repayment obligations and repay the principal and interest of your bank's loan on time. If the company defaults or delays repayment of the loan principal and interest to your bank, this government will be responsible for resolving the matter and will not allow your bank to suffer economic losses."

On October 24, 1996, Foshan Municipal Government issued a "Letter of Undertaking" numbered Fo Fu Han (1996) No. 144 to Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications, stating: "Zhongya Company is an institution of our city stationed in Hong Kong. In order to further develop the company's foreign trade business, the company hereby applies to your bank for the following banking facilities: a mortgage loan of HKD 62.62 million secured by the properties on the 16th, 17th and 18th floors located at Morrison Hill Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, with a term of two years. The above-mentioned application has been approved by our city government upon study. Please provide support to the company stationed in Hong Kong in accordance with its actual business development needs. This government is willing to urge the company stationed in Hong Kong to faithfully perform its repayment obligations and repay the principal and interest of your bank's loan on time. If the company defaults or delays repayment of the loan principal and interest to your bank, this government will be responsible for resolving the matter and will not allow your bank to suffer economic losses."

On October 30, 1996, Foshan Municipal Government issued a "Letter of Undertaking" numbered Fo Fu Han (1996) No. 146 to Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications, stating: "Peak Garden Limited (hereinafter referred to as Peak Garden Company) is an institution of our city stationed in Hong Kong. In order to further develop the company's foreign trade business, the company hereby applies to your bank for the following banking facilities: a mortgage loan of HKD 61.5 million secured by the properties on the 11th, 12th and 15th floors located at Morrison Hill Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, with a term of two years. The above-mentioned application has been approved by our city government upon study. Please provide support to the company stationed in Hong Kong in accordance with its actual business development needs. This government is willing to urge the company stationed in Hong Kong to faithfully perform its repayment obligations and repay the principal and interest of your bank's loan on time. If the company defaults or delays repayment of the loan principal and interest to your bank, this government will be responsible for resolving the matter and will not allow your bank to suffer economic losses."

On May 20, 1996, Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications issued a letter to Zhongya Company regarding the provision of credit facilities, stating: The bank credit currently being provided to Zhongya Company is revised as follows: Limits: (1) Overdraft facility of HKD 3 million, with interest calculated at the bank's prime lending rate plus 2% per annum, to be deducted monthly from Zhongya Company's current account. (2) Installment loans of HKD 1.548 million and HKD 1.017 million respectively, with existing repayment terms and conditions unchanged. (3) Term loan of HKD 19 million (this facility should be used to repay the HKD 25 million term loan and the HKD 6 million overdraft), with interest calculated at 10.5% per annum (subject to fluctuation), calculated on the daily outstanding balance and payable monthly. The principal must be fully repaid on or before April 30, 1997. (4) Letter of credit (including 90-day trust receipt of HKD 20 million) of HKD 30 million. (5) Term loan of HKD 5 million, with existing repayment terms and conditions unchanged. Interest shall be calculated daily on the basis of actual days and a 365-day year. For instruments with a tenor of less than 90 days, interest at the bank's prime lending rate plus 1% per annum; for 91 to 150 days, at the bank's prime lending rate plus 3.5% per annum; for over 150 days, at the bank's prime lending rate plus 5.5% per annum. Upon signing this letter, a handling fee of HKD 47,500 shall be deducted from Zhongya Company's current account, and other corresponding handling fees shall be determined at the discretion of this bank. The aforementioned bank credit shall be available upon Zhongya Company's acceptance and full compliance with the terms and conditions set forth in this letter, and upon completion of all documents deemed appropriate by this bank, until the inspection date set forth below or such other time as notified in writing by this bank. This bank will review the above credit terms on or before June 30, 1996. Zhongya Company signed the above letter and indicated acceptance of the above terms and conditions.

On July 16, 1996, Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications issued a letter to Zhongya Company regarding the provision of credit facilities, stating: The bank credit currently being provided to Zhongya Company is revised as follows: Limits: (1) Overdraft facility of HKD 3 million, with interest calculated at the bank's prime lending rate plus 2% per annum, to be deducted monthly from Zhongya Company's current account. (2) Installment loan of HKD 1.548 million. (3) Term loans of HKD 5 million, HKD 19 million and HKD 43 million respectively, with existing repayment terms and conditions unchanged. (4) Letter of credit (including 90-day trust receipt of HKD 20 million) of HKD 30 million. Interest shall be calculated daily on the basis of actual days and a 365-day year. For instruments with a tenor of less than 90 days, interest at the bank's prime lending rate plus 1% per annum; for 91 to 150 days, at the bank's prime lending rate plus 3.5% per annum; for over 150 days, at the bank's prime lending rate plus 5.5% per annum. Upon signing this letter, a handling fee of HKD 57,500 shall be deducted from Zhongya Company's current account, and other corresponding handling fees shall be determined at the discretion of this bank. The aforementioned bank credit shall be available upon Zhongya Company's acceptance and full compliance with the terms and conditions set forth in this letter, and upon completion of all documents deemed appropriate by this bank, until the inspection date set forth below or such other time as notified in writing by this bank. This bank will review the above credit terms on or before June 30, 1997. Zhongya Company signed the above letter and indicated acceptance of the above terms and conditions.

On October 25, 1996, Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications issued a letter to Zhongya Company regarding the provision of credit facilities, stating: In addition to the bank credit currently being provided to Zhongya Company, a credit limit will be provided as follows: Term loan of HKD 62.62 million, with a term of 12 months, interest calculated at 10.5% per annum (subject to fluctuation), calculated on the daily outstanding balance and payable monthly; interest for the first three months (amounting to HKD 1,643,775) shall be paid to this bank at the time of the loan disbursement; interest for the fourth, fifth and sixth months (amounting to HKD 1,643,775) shall be paid to this bank on or before November 30, 1996; thereafter, interest for subsequent months shall be paid to this bank monthly. Interest shall be calculated daily on the basis of actual days and a 365-day year. Guarantee includes a letter of undertaking issued by Foshan Municipal Government for this loan. Upon signing this letter, a handling fee of HKD 313,100 (if any) shall be collected by the bank's legal counsel, and other corresponding handling fees shall be determined at the discretion of this bank. The aforementioned bank credit shall be available upon Zhongya Company's acceptance and full compliance with the terms and conditions set forth in this letter, and upon completion of all documents deemed appropriate by this bank, until the inspection date set forth below or such other time as notified in writing by this bank. Zhongya Company signed the above letter and indicated acceptance of the above terms and conditions.

On December 11, 1998, Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications issued a "Credit Agreement" letter numbered LC-1998-0931-COM-2473 to Zhongya Company regarding the provision of credit facilities, stating: The loan credit currently being provided to Zhongya Company, with a principal amount of HKD 77,438,282.02 (including overdraft credit balance of HKD 918,682.02, term loan credit balance of HKD 62.62 million, and letter of credit [trust receipt] credit balance of HKD 13,899,600) will be revised as follows: (a) The accrued interest on the said loan of HKD 12,790,750.63 shall be capitalized as principal and, for administrative reasons, recorded in a loan account with a separate account number; and (b) the repayment period of the loan credit (including the capitalized interest) shall be extended as follows: (1) Overdraft facility (outstanding principal amount) of HKD 918,682.02, with an overdraft annual interest rate calculated at the higher of (a) overnight interbank offered rate, or (b) the bank's prime lending rate plus 2.5%, or (c) deposit rate plus 1% (referring to deposits pledged to the bank), to be deducted from Zhongya Company's account on the last business day of each month. The principal shall be fully repaid on the date falling two years from the date of disbursement. (2) Term loan (outstanding principal amount) of HKD 62.62 million, with interest charged at the bank's prime lending rate plus 2.5% per annum, payable annually. The principal shall be fully repaid on the date falling two years from the date of disbursement. (3) Letter of credit (trust receipt) of HKD 13,899,600, with interest charged on the drawings under the import documents at the bank's current rate, payable annually, deducted from Zhongya Company's current account, with the principal fully repaid on the date falling two years from the date of disbursement. (4) Term loan (capitalized interest) of HKD 12,790,750.63, with interest charged at the bank's prime lending rate plus 2.5% per annum, payable annually, with the principal fully repaid on the date falling two years from the date of disbursement. Interest shall be calculated daily on the basis of actual days and a 365-day year. For any overdue amounts under the term loan, this bank is entitled to charge overdue interest at an annual rate of the bank's prime lending rate plus 4.25%. Interest shall be calculated from the date of default until the actual full repayment of the outstanding amount. However, this bank may change the basis for calculating overdue interest by displaying or posting a notice in the bank's lobby for 30 days at any time. For any overdue amounts under the overdraft facility, this bank is entitled to charge overdue interest at an annual rate of the overnight interbank offered rate or the bank's prime lending rate plus 9%. Interest shall be calculated from the date of default until the actual full repayment of the outstanding amount. However, this bank may change the basis for calculating overdue interest by displaying or posting a notice in the bank's lobby for 30 days at any time, etc. Guarantee includes a letter of undertaking issued by Foshan Municipal Government. The aforementioned bank credit shall be available upon Zhongya Company's acceptance and full compliance with the terms and conditions set forth in this letter, and upon completion of all documents deemed appropriate by this bank, until such other time as notified in writing by this bank. This letter is supplementary in nature. This letter is governed by the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and shall be construed in all respects in accordance with the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Zhongya Company hereby irrevocably submits to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, but this bank shall have the right to enforce this letter in any other court of competent jurisdiction of its choice, etc. Zhongya Company signed the above letter and indicated that after due and careful consideration of the contents of this letter, it agreed to accept the credit facility and be bound by all the terms and conditions set forth in this letter.

On October 29, 1996, Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications issued a letter to Peak Garden Company regarding the provision of credit facilities, stating: In addition to the bank credit currently being provided to Peak Garden Company, a credit limit will be provided as follows: Term loan of HKD 61.5 million, with a term of 12 months, interest calculated at 12% per annum (subject to fluctuation), calculated on the daily outstanding balance and payable monthly; interest for the first three months (amounting to HKD 1,614,375) shall be paid to this bank at the time of the loan disbursement; interest for the fourth, fifth and sixth months (amounting to HKD 1,614,375) shall be paid to this bank on or before November 30, 1996; thereafter, interest for subsequent months shall be paid to this bank monthly. Interest shall be calculated daily on the basis of actual days and a 365-day year. Guarantee includes a letter of undertaking from Foshan Municipal Government. Upon signing this letter, a handling fee of HKD 307,500 (if any) shall be collected by the bank's legal counsel, and other corresponding handling fees shall be determined at the discretion of this bank. The aforementioned bank credit shall be available upon Peak Garden Company's acceptance and full compliance with the terms and conditions set forth in this letter, and upon completion of all documents deemed appropriate by this bank, until the inspection date set forth below or such other time as notified in writing by this bank. Peak Garden Company signed the above letter and indicated acceptance of the above terms and conditions.

On April 18, 1997, Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications issued a letter to Peak Garden Company regarding the provision of credit facilities, stating: In addition to the bank credit currently being provided to Peak Garden Company, a credit limit will be provided as follows: Term loan of HKD 9 million, with a term of 6 months, interest calculated at 10.75% per annum (subject to fluctuation), calculated on the daily outstanding balance and payable monthly; the principal must be repaid upon the expiry of 6 months from the date of disbursement. Interest shall be calculated daily on the basis of actual days and a 365-day year. Upon signing this letter, a handling fee of HKD 22,500 shall be deducted from Peak Garden Company's current account, and other corresponding handling fees shall be determined at the discretion of this bank. The aforementioned bank credit shall be available upon Peak Garden Company's acceptance and full compliance with the terms and conditions set forth in this letter, and upon completion of all documents deemed appropriate by this bank, until the inspection date set forth below or such other time as notified in writing by this bank. Peak Garden Company signed the above letter and indicated acceptance of the above terms and conditions.

On December 11, 1998, Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications issued a "Credit Agreement" letter numbered LC-1998-0929-COM-2473 to Peak Garden Company regarding the provision of credit facilities, stating: The loan credit currently being provided to Peak Garden Company, with a principal amount of HKD 61.5 million, will be revised as follows: (a) The accrued interest on the said loan of HKD 10,536,282.7 shall be capitalized as principal and, for administrative reasons, recorded in a loan account with a separate account number; and (b) the repayment period of the loan credit (including the capitalized interest) shall be extended as follows: (1) The original principal amount of HKD 61.5 million shall have interest charged at the bank's prime lending rate plus 2.5%, payable annually. The principal shall be fully repaid on the date falling two years from the date of disbursement. (2) The capitalized interest of HKD 10,536,282.7 shall have interest charged at the bank's prime lending rate plus 2.5%, payable annually. The principal shall be fully repaid on the date falling two years from the date of disbursement. Interest shall be calculated daily on the basis of actual days and a 365-day year. For any overdue amounts under the term loan, this bank is entitled to charge overdue interest at an annual rate of the bank's prime lending rate plus 4.25%. Interest shall be calculated from the date of default until the actual full repayment of the outstanding amount. However, this bank may change the basis for calculating overdue interest by displaying or posting a notice in the bank's lobby for 30 days at any time. For any overdue amounts under the overdraft facility, this bank is entitled to charge overdue interest at an annual rate of the overnight interbank offered rate or the bank's prime lending rate plus 9%. Interest shall be calculated from the date of default until the actual full repayment of the outstanding amount. However, this bank may change the basis for calculating overdue interest by displaying or posting a notice in the bank's lobby for 30 days at any time, etc. Guarantee includes a letter of undertaking issued by Foshan Municipal Government. The aforementioned bank credit shall be available upon Peak Garden Company's acceptance and full compliance with the terms and conditions set forth in this letter, and upon completion of all documents deemed appropriate by this bank, until such other time as notified in writing by this bank. This letter is supplementary in nature. This letter is governed by the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and shall be construed in all respects in accordance with the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Peak Garden Company hereby irrevocably submits to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, but this bank shall have the right to enforce this letter in any other court of competent jurisdiction of its choice, etc. Peak Garden Company signed the above letter and indicated that after due and careful consideration of the contents of this letter, it agreed to accept the credit facility and be bound by all the terms and conditions set forth in this letter.

As of December 23, 1998, Zhongya Company, and as of December 23, 1999, Peak Garden Company, were still making interest payments on the overdue amounts to Hong Kong Branch of Bank of Communications from their respective accounts.

On August 9, 2000, the Hong Kong Official Receiver's Office, based on the application of Hong Kong Bank of Communications (HK BoCom), issued a winding-up order against Central Asia Company. As of April 24, 2001, the total amount owed by Central Asia Company to HK BoCom was HKD 86,896,642.21 (Note: this amount was calculated in advance by deducting the mortgaged property value at an estimated value of HKD 1.3 million, whereas the actual amount realized was HKD 889,320; therefore, the current creditor's right of HK BoCom against Central Asia Company is HKD 87,307,322.21). On March 7, 2002, the High Court of Hong Kong, by Final Judgment No. 4924 of 2001, ordered Jingshan Company to pay to HK BoCom: (1) HKD 78,293,395.48; (2) interest on the principal of HKD 61.5 million at an annual rate of 9.75% or at a daily rate of HKD 16,428.08 until full repayment; (3) interest on the principal of HKD 4,907,870.91 at an annual rate of 9.75% or at a daily rate of HKD 1,311.01 from October 20, 2001 until the date of this judgment, and thereafter at the court's judgment rate until full repayment; (4) interest on the principal of HKD 2,481,571.07 at the court's judgment rate from September 1, 2000 until the date of this judgment, and thereafter at the court's judgment rate until full repayment; (5) fixed litigation costs of HKD 1,745.

The "Minutes of the 1998 Symposium between Foshan Municipal Government Leaders and Hong Kong Bank of Communications Leaders" recorded: On the afternoon of February 19, 1998, Foshan Municipal Government Mayor Liang Shaotang, Deputy Mayor Lu Hanchao, Deputy Mayor Liu Gengwen, Deputy Mayor Huang Zhenhui, Mayor's Assistant Li Jingyuan, and HK BoCom Deputy General Manager Liu Jianxin, Deputy General Manager Liu Yuanbiao, and responsible persons from relevant departments of both sides held a meeting at the First Guesthouse of Foshan Municipal Government concerning the business dealings and existing problems between Foshan municipal direct enterprises and HK BoCom. Both sides candidly exchanged views and reached the following four points of consensus: 1. Foshan City and HK BoCom have been mutually supportive and have developed together over the past 20 years. Both sides believe that they should continue to actively, steadily, and effectively provide strong support to Foshan's enterprises. Foshan Municipal Government and HK BoCom will strengthen communication and collaboration to further develop the partnership and cooperative relationship between Foshan City and HK BoCom, thereby contributing to the national economic cause. 2. Some individual enterprises in Foshan have encountered economic difficulties due to investment decision-making errors in previous years and the impact of the mainland's triangular debt problem, failing to repay bank loans on schedule, which has caused the bank to attract attention from Hong Kong regulatory authorities on how to properly handle related credit. Regarding this, the Municipal Government will coordinate relevant parties, adopt effective measures to help enterprises overcome difficulties, and reasonably repay bank loans in different ways relative to the original credit terms. In addition, the Municipal Government will, at an appropriate time, carry out asset restructuring of enterprises, by establishing new companies, injecting high-quality assets, improving the economic efficiency of enterprises, and resolving existing debts. 3. Due to the Asian financial crisis, Hong Kong's economy has been severely affected, and the business environment for enterprises has deteriorated. HK BoCom expressed understanding of this, and adhering to the attitude of "first urge, second help, third cooperate," will continue to support the development of Foshan enterprises, assist relevant enterprises in debt restructuring, resolve existing problems through friendly consultation, and for newly established enterprises and injected projects, as long as they are beneficial, have promising development prospects, and comply with the regulatory norms of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, will provide strong support under the principles of "reasonableness, fairness, and legality." 4. Both sides agreed to continue cooperation on projects that are in line with national industrial policies and are beneficial.

The "Minutes of the 1998 Symposium between Foshan Mayor Liang Shaotang and Hong Kong Bank of Communications (Second Session)" recorded the following: On the afternoon of August 19, Foshan Mayor Liang Shaotang, Deputy Mayor Huang Zhenhui, Mayor's Assistant and Director of the Foshan Municipal Overseas Work Leading Group Office Li Jingyuan and Deputy Director Xiao Jianwei, along with HK BoCom Deputy General Manager Liu Jianxin, Deputy General Manager Liu Yuanbiao, Senior Manager Yan Songchang, Deputy Manager Guan Shaohong, and Deputy Manager Pan Weixing, successively held meetings at the First Guesthouse of Foshan Municipal Government concerning the business dealings and unresolved issues between Foshan municipal enterprises and HK BoCom. Both sides candidly exchanged information and opinions and reached the following four points of consensus: 1. Based on the minutes of the first symposium on February 19, 1998, HK BoCom reported the situation and reiterated that it will continue to adhere to the attitude of "first urge, second help, third cooperate" and the purpose of "mutual support and common development" in dealing with Foshan Municipal Government related companies under the new circumstances. The Foshan side truthfully reflected its own recent situation. Through communication, both sides agreed to intensify efforts to rationalize the unresolved debts of Foshan municipal enterprises to HK BoCom under the new circumstances, to tide over difficulties together, and agreed to take "mutual support, tide over difficulties together, and common development" as their common goal. 2. The Asian financial crisis has not only affected Hong Kong and other Asian countries but has further impacted the whole world. Under such an economic environment, the difficulty of solving problems has increased. However, the Municipal Government, with an attitude of being responsible to the bank, sincerely intends to develop cooperation with HK BoCom based on many years of cooperative relations. Taking into account the different circumstances of each enterprise unit, it will adopt a "one key opens one lock" approach, analyzing each case specifically, and solving them one by one in a practical and realistic manner under the principles of "reasonableness, fairness, and legality." The Municipal Government will provide full coordination and balance. 3. For some enterprises under the Foshan Government, as long as the projects and businesses meet the criteria of "having market, prospects, policies, and benefits" and the relevant standards of banking regulators, the bank will continue to provide financing and increase their "hematopoietic function." However, this will be operated in the form of "debt financing," i.e., establishing a new company to assume the debt, with funds used for specific purposes only, to prevent the original company from being drained of funds by creditor banks or entities, thereby "bleeding continuously," and also to enable the financing bank to play the role of a "company doctor" for blood transfusion, conditioning, and monitoring. This is in the interests of the Municipal Government, the enterprise units, and the financing bank, achieving a win-win situation. Both sides agreed to implement the specific methods as soon as possible within the year by establishing new companies, injecting relevant good businesses and projects, gradually injecting good assets, and combining various financing methods to promote the profitability of the new companies, thereby resolving existing debts and the conditioning work of the original enterprises. Which specific companies are suitable for this method will be determined through further consultation between the two sides. 4. Under the current economic environment, it will take a relatively long time to completely solve all problems. In order to coordinate the work of all parties, both sides agreed to implement a quarterly liaison meeting (initiated before restructuring, and may be convened at any time with mutual consent) organized by a group headed by Mayor's Assistant Li Jingyuan on the Foshan side and a group headed by a deputy general manager on the HK BoCom side. The purpose is to inspect and report on the implementation and progress of the restructuring plan. Issues that cannot be resolved at the liaison meeting may be referred to the responsible Deputy Mayor for resolution. On October 13, 1998, the Foshan Municipal Government and HK BoCom signed and sealed these minutes.

On November 12, 1998, the Foshan Municipal Foreign Economic and Trade Commission (hereinafter referred to as Foshan Foreign Economic Commission) issued Document No. Fo Jing Mao Fa [1998] 42 to Delta Development Co., Ltd., titled "Reply on Agreeing Delta Development Co., Ltd. to Pledge Part of the Equity Interests in Baihua Plaza as Collateral," which stated: We have received your company's report dated November 11, 1998, regarding the handling opinions on the overdue loans owed by Central Asia, Jingshan, Bubu Jia, and Delta Companies to HK BoCom. Upon study, it is agreed that you may pledge the 30% equity interests held by your company in Baihua Plaza as collateral to HK BoCom, and this shall be used for the debt restructuring of the aforementioned companies.

The "Minutes of the Meeting between Foshan Municipal Foreign Economic and Trade Commission and Hong Kong Bank of Communications on November 12, 1998" recorded: Meeting location: Fourth floor conference room of Foshan Municipal Foreign Economic and Trade Commission. Attendees: Luo Yuetang and Chen Jianzhong of Foshan Foreign Economic Commission; Liang Jinglin and Wang Wei of Delta Development Co., Ltd.; Lin Jingxiong of Central Asia Enterprise Co., Ltd.; Zhang Wenjun and Liang Kaiming of Bubu Jia Enterprise Co., Ltd.; Yan Songchang and Pan Weixing of HK BoCom. Content: Luo Yuetang: During the current difficult period for Hong Kong's economy, all companies stationed in Hong Kong under the Foreign Economic Commission have overdue loans from Bank of Communications. However, with the understanding of the bank and under the coordination of the city leadership, it is agreed to use Delta's 30% equity in Baihua Plaza as collateral to restructure the debts of the relevant companies. In the previous stage, Liang Jinglin and the bank have done a lot of work, but everyone's cooperation and assistance are still needed to ensure the successful completion of the debt restructuring work.

Yan Songchang: Given that the bank must disclose the provision for doubtful debts by the end of this year as required by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, and disclose non-performing assets next year, the total loan amount in the Foshan area reaches HKD 1 billion, of which 50% are problematic. Therefore, the bank faces huge provisioning, affecting the bank's asset structure and rating, and even affecting the image of Foshan. Our bank has a 20-year relationship with Foshan, and the relationship is very good. Regarding the debt restructuring of Foshan companies, we have been in contact with Foshan mayors and deputy mayors many times, and have reached consensus on some principles of debt restructuring, which have been recorded in meeting minutes. With the active support of General Manager Liang, the relevant collateral documents have been signed despite difficulties. This morning, with the support of Director Luo, an immediate approval for the collateral was given. After the meeting, the relevant documents will be handed over to Jinxin Law Firm for registration. We hope that through this meeting, we can explain our ideas to everyone and communicate, to ensure that the accounts of each company are handled by the end of this month. For companies under the Foreign Economic Commission, all use Delta's equity in Baihua Plaza as collateral to carry out a series of debt restructurings. Although this method carries higher risk for the bank, we hope to use the equity collateral as a means to buy time for the debt restructuring of some companies, hoping to gradually solve the problems or find other solutions during the period. On the other hand, in the spirit of "first urge, second help, third cooperate," we will give "hematopoietic function" to companies that still have operational capabilities, support them to generate profits, reduce liabilities. However, for companies granted new credit, our bank will send personnel to conduct on-site audits of company accounts, understand the latest operational situation of the company, provide opinions and market information on some new trade transactions, ensure that trade transactions no longer experience errors, protect both parties, and prevent misappropriation of funds and a repetition of past mistakes.

Lin Jingxiong: In the past, the bank assisted us with credit investigations for trade, which helped to understand the counterparty.

Pan Weixing: First, introduce the bank's debt restructuring plan for each company. It is mainly divided into two major groups: "Delta" and "Central Asia." Central Asia has already established a new company, Peishun, and another new company needs to be established for restructuring. Since some companies are considering loans in the form of working capital, supporting information must be provided. Therefore, please ask General Manager Liang to provide information on relevant investment projects and arrange for colleagues from the Industrial and Commercial Services Department to come to Foshan next week to consider relevant projects and deepen understanding.

Liang Jinglin: Agree to the restructuring plan proposed by Bank of Communications. Relevant projects can be obtained directly from Wang Wei. Additionally, although each company belongs to the foreign economic system, they are independent legal entities. For financial accountability purposes, each company is required to sign a debt guarantee letter of commitment to Delta. Each attending representative expressed no objection to the debt restructuring method proposed by Bank of Communications at the meeting. The Foshan Municipal Foreign Economic and Trade Commission and HK BoCom signed this record.

Foshan Municipal Government submitted two "Comfort Letters" dated December 25, 1998, addressed to HK BoCom, with reference numbers Fo Fu Han (1998) 067 and 068, which stated: Central Asia Company and Jingshan Company are enterprises stationed in Hong Kong under our city, directly under the leadership of the Foshan Municipal Foreign Economic and Trade Commission. These companies have applied for banking facilities from your bank for operational needs. Due to adverse economic factors in Hong Kong, they have defaulted on loan principal and interest owed to your bank. With the support of your bank, these companies are now undergoing debt restructuring. This government is aware of the relevant debt restructuring. This government will continue to be responsible for supervising these companies to repay the loan principal and interest to your bank in accordance with the debt restructuring agreement. However, HK BoCom did not acknowledge receipt of these two "Comfort Letters." During the trial at first instance, Foshan Municipal Government also failed to provide evidence proving that HK BoCom had received these two "Comfort Letters."

The court of first instance found after trial: This case is an action brought by the lender HK BoCom against the guarantor Foshan Municipal Government, and is a dispute over a Hong Kong-related guarantee contract. By order of the Supreme People's Court, the court of first instance has jurisdiction over this case.

This case is a dispute over a Hong Kong-related guarantee contract. Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's "Answers to Certain Issues Concerning the Trial of Economic Dispute Cases Involving Hong Kong and Macau" and other judicial interpretations, in the trial of economic dispute cases involving Hong Kong, the procedural provisions of the Foreign-related Section of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China shall apply, meaning that such cases shall be handled by analogy with foreign-related cases. The parties in this case did not agree on the law applicable to the contractual dispute. Since the location of the defendant, the place of conclusion of the guarantee contract, and the place of performance are all within Mainland China, pursuant to Article 145 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, applying the principle of the closest connection, the law of Mainland China shall apply to this case.

Based on the facts on which the plaintiff's action is based, this case comprises two legal relationships. One is that HK BoCom provided loans (credit) to Central Asia Company, and Foshan Municipal Government issued a letter of commitment for such loans (credit). The other is that HK BoCom provided loans (credit) to Jingshan Company, and Foshan Municipal Government issued a letter of commitment for such loans (credit). According to the registration materials of Central Asia Company and Jingshan Company, they are two different legal persons and not the same entity. The act of HK BoCom in providing loans (credit) to Central Asia Company and Jingshan Company respectively constitutes two different legal relationships. The act of Foshan Municipal Government in issuing letters of commitment for Central Asia Company and Jingshan Company respectively also constitutes separate legal relationships. Article 126 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If the plaintiff adds claims, the defendant files a counterclaim, or a third party files a claim related to the case, the court may consolidate the trials." Given that the plaintiff in this case makes claims against the defendant for two guarantee acts, and the subject matter is the same type, the court of first instance decided to consolidate the trials based on the principle of litigation efficiency.

HK BoCom's claim is: "Request the court to order Foshan Municipal Government to bear civil liability for compensation of one-half to the extent of the part of the debts of Central Asia Company and Jingshan Company that they cannot repay." The basis of the claim is that Foshan Municipal Government promised in the "Letter of Commitment": "This government is willing to urge the said companies stationed in Hong Kong to earnestly fulfill their repayment obligations and repay the loan principal and interest to your bank on time. If such companies fail to repay or default on the loan principal and interest to your bank, this government will be responsible for resolving the matter and will not cause economic losses to your bank." Clearly, HK BoCom requests Foshan Municipal Government to bear compensation liability for an invalid guarantee. Therefore, the focus of the dispute in this case is: Does the letter of commitment issued by Foshan Municipal Government constitute a guarantee?

In this case, whether the letter of commitment issued by Foshan Municipal Government has the effect of a guarantee instrument shall be determined based on the content of the letter of commitment. The so-called suretyship refers to an expression of intent by a third party agreeing with the creditor that, when the debtor fails to perform its obligations, the third party will perform the debt or bear liability in accordance with the agreement. The core of a suretyship is that the surety has the intent to repay the debt on behalf of the debtor. In the "Letters of Commitment" issued on May 8, 1994 (Fo Fu Han [1994] No. 030), and on October 30, 1996 (Fo Fu Han [1996] No. 144 and Fo Fu Han [1996] No. 146), Foshan Municipal Government clearly stated: If Central Asia Company or Jingshan Company defaults on or fails to repay loan principal and interest, Foshan Municipal Government will be responsible for resolving the matter and will not cause HK BoCom economic losses. This promise by Foshan Municipal Government clearly expresses the intention to repay the debts on behalf of Central Asia Company and Jingshan Company. Foshan Municipal Government contends that these letters of commitment are comfort letters, not guarantee letters. Admittedly, in international financial dealings, it is common for a third party to issue a comfort letter to the lender. It is a written statement sent by the third party to the creditor, indicating that the third party assumes a moral obligation for the debtor's repayment, or that an affiliate company guarantees the debtor's business and asset status, or urges the debtor to repay the debt. A comfort letter is not a guarantee contract, but as a written expression, it has similarities to a guarantee contract. In special circumstances, a comfort letter can also constitute a guarantee contract, i.e., a special comfort letter may become a form of guarantee contract. Thus, the concept of a comfort letter does not have an independent or precise legal meaning. Being identified as a comfort letter does not necessarily mean it does not constitute a guarantee. Moreover, being identified as a comfort letter does not mean that the issuer of the letter bears no legal liability when the situation guaranteed by the letter changes and causes the creditor's claims to become unenforceable. The validity and effect of a written document called a comfort letter depend on its content. The first part of the letter of commitment in this case indeed has the general meaning of a comfort letter, but the latter part clearly, as described above, contains content regarding repayment on behalf of the debtor or assuming guarantee obligations, and should be regarded as an expression of intent to provide a guarantee. The argument of Foshan Municipal Government that the letter of commitment it issued is a comfort letter and does not have the nature of a guarantee is not supported by sufficient reasons and is not upheld. Therefore, in this case, there exists a legal relationship of guarantee between Foshan Municipal Government and HK BoCom, and the dispute between them is a Hong Kong-related guarantee contract dispute. Consequently, the commitment of Foshan Municipal Government reflects the intent to provide a guarantee for the loans of Central Asia Company and Jingshan Company, which is consistent with the spirit of Article 6 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China. It should be determined that Foshan Municipal Government provided a guarantee for the loans of Central Asia Company and Jingshan Company to HK BoCom.

Since in this case none of the Letters of Undertaking specified a guarantee period or identified which particular loan they secured, but instead agreed to provide a guarantee within the credit line, a dispute arose between the parties as to whether this guarantee constituted a maximum amount suretyship or a guarantee for a specific loan. The undertakings in this case were provided as guarantees for the letters of credit offered by Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch to Zhongya Company and Jingshan Company. The letters of credit did not provide for a specific loan, but rather constituted a loan commitment from the lender limiting the maximum loan balance. Therefore, when the Foshan Municipal Government issued to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch on May 8, 1994 and October 30, 1996 the Letters of Undertaking numbered Fo Fu Han (1994) No. 030, Fo Fu Han (1996) No. 144, and Fo Fu Han (1996) No. 146, these were in fact providing guarantees for the amounts under the letters of credit issued by Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch to Zhongya Company and Jingshan Company on May 20, 1996, July 6, 1996, and April 18, 1997 respectively. The scope of the guarantee provided should be the loans extended under the letters of credit issued by Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch on the basis of those Letters of Undertaking, i.e., the loans disbursed by Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch to Zhongya Company and Jingshan Company pursuant to its letters of credit. In this case, the Foshan Municipal Government argued in its defense that the loans referred to in the Letters of Undertaking were unrelated to the loans sued upon by the plaintiff, and that it had no obligation to assume liability for the loans sued upon. This argument cannot stand and is not supported by the court of first instance. The maximum amount suretyship established by the Foshan Municipal Government based on the Fo Fu Han (1994) No. 030, Fo Fu Han (1996) No. 144, and Fo Fu Han (1996) No. 146 Letters of Undertaking issued on May 8, 1994 and October 30, 1996 constitutes an external guarantee. The Foshan Municipal Government is a state government organ, and its provision of an external guarantee violates the prohibitive provision of Article 8 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China that state organs shall not act as guarantors. At the same time, according to the provision of Article 6, paragraph 2 of the Measures for the Administration of External Guarantees Provided by Domestic Institutions promulgated by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange in 1991, "The provision of foreign exchange guarantees for enterprises stationed abroad by Chinese entities shall be subject to the approval of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange," an external guarantee requires approval to become effective. Since the procedures for approval of an external guarantee were not completed in this case, this violates the provision of Article 58 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China that "The following civil acts are void: ... (5) Those that violate the law or public interest; ..." and the provision of Article 6 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China that "An external guarantee shall be void under any of the following circumstances: (1) Where the guarantee has not been approved or registered by the competent state authority." Therefore, the guarantee acts constituted by the above Letters of Undertaking do not have the legally binding force of a valid guarantee. The responsibility for the invalidity of the guarantee in this case lies with Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch and the Foshan Municipal Government. According to Article 61, paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China: "After a civil act has been confirmed as void or rescinded, the property acquired by a party as a result of the act shall be returned to the party who suffered the loss. The party at fault shall compensate the other party for the losses incurred as a result thereof; if both parties are at fault, they shall each bear their respective liability." And according to Article 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China: "Where the principal contract is valid but the guaranty contract is void, and the creditor is not at fault, the guarantor and the debtor shall bear joint and several compensatory liability for the economic losses of the creditor under the principal contract; if both the creditor and the guarantor are at fault, the portion of civil liability to be borne by the guarantor shall not exceed one-half of the portion that the debtor is unable to satisfy." The Foshan Municipal Government shall bear compensatory liability for one-half of the portion that the debtor is unable to satisfy. Since the Foshan Municipal Government raised no objection to the calculation of the amount of principal and interest of the debts that Zhongya Company and Jingshan Company are unable to satisfy, the court of first instance confirmed that amount. Therefore, the Foshan Municipal Government shall bear compensatory liability for one-half of the portion of the principal debt of HKD 87,307,322.21 and interest (calculated according to the provisions of Credit Facility Agreements LC-1998-0929-COM-2473 and LC-1998-0931-COM-2473 from April 24, 2001 until full repayment) owed by Zhongya Company to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch, and the portion of the principal debt of HKD 78,293,395.48 and interest (calculated at the interest rate confirmed by Final Judgment No. 4924 of 2001 of the High Court of Hong Kong from October 20, 2001 until full repayment) owed by Jingshan Company to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch, that the debtors are unable to satisfy.

As for the fact that after Zhongya Company and Jingshan Company failed to repay their debts to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch on time, the Foshan Municipal Government and Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch successively held consultations and produced the "Minutes of the Symposium between Foshan Municipal Government Leaders and Leaders of Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch in 1998", the "Minutes of the Second Symposium between Foshan Mayor Liang Shaotang and Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch in 1998", and the "Minutes of the Meeting between Foshan Foreign Economic Relations and Trade Commission and Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch on November 12, 1998", all of which were signed and confirmed by the Foshan Municipal Government and Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch. These indicated a continued effort to resolve the debt issues between Zhongya Company, Jingshan Company, and Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch, and expressed agreement with Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch's restructuring plan. On December 11, 1998, Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch and Zhongya Company signed Credit Facility Agreement LC-1998-0931-COM-2473 under the restructuring plan, which included a term credit facility of HKD 62.62 million; Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch and Jingshan Company signed Credit Facility Agreement LC-1998-0929-COM-2473 under the restructuring plan, which included a credit line of HKD 61.5 million. Both of these contracts, in Article 3 "Collateral and Legal Documents to be Provided", included "Letter of Undertaking issued by Foshan Municipal Government". It can be seen that the Credit Facility Agreements concluded between Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch and Zhongya Company and Jingshan Company due to the debt restructuring did not expand the scope of the Foshan Municipal Government's commitment to repay the original loans of HKD 62.62 million and HKD 61.5 million to Zhongya Company and Jingshan Company, nor did they waive the Letters of Undertaking issued by the Foshan Municipal Government. Therefore, the signing of the above minutes and Credit Facility Agreements cannot change the act of the Foshan Municipal Government providing a guarantee to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch.

Another focus of dispute in this case is whether the claim of Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch has exceeded the statutory limitation of action. In this case, the liability borne by the Foshan Municipal Government is a compensatory liability arising from an invalid guarantee. Therefore, the limitation period for the claim for such compensation cannot be calculated based on the guarantee period and limitation of action applicable to a valid guarantee. Since the determination of compensatory liability for an invalid guarantee depends on the determination of the portion of the principal debt that the debtor is unable to satisfy, it is certain that if the limitation period for the principal debt has not expired, the limitation period for the claim seeking compensation from the guarantor for the invalid guarantee has also not expired. The facts of this case show that on December 11, 1998, Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch reconfirmed the claims and debts in this case with Zhongya Company and Jingshan Company through Credit Facility Agreements LC-1998-0931-COM-2473 and LC-1998-0929-COM-2473 respectively, and stipulated a loan term of two years, meaning the maturity date of the principal debt was December 11, 2000. Moreover, both Credit Facility Agreements LC-1998-0931-COM-2473 and LC-1998-0929-COM-2473 stipulated that Hong Kong law should apply. According to Article 4 of the Limitation Ordinance of Hong Kong: "Limitation of actions founded on contract and tort and certain other actions (1) The following actions shall not be brought after the expiration of 6 years from the date on which the cause of action accrued: (a) actions founded on simple contract or tort; ..." The limitation period for the principal debt in this case commenced from the last agreed repayment date above and extended for six years. In fact, on August 9, 2000, the Official Receiver's Office of Hong Kong issued a winding-up order against Zhongya Company upon the application of Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch. On March 7, 2002, the High Court of Hong Kong, by Final Judgment No. 4924 of 2001, determined the debt of Jingshan Company to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch. That is to say, the limitation period for the principal debt had not expired. Therefore, the filing of this lawsuit by Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch with the court of first instance on December 14, 2000, also did not exceed the limitation period. The Foshan Municipal Government's assertion that the claim of Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch exceeded the limitation period is not supported by the court of first instance.

As for the two Comfort Letters provided by the Foshan Municipal Government, since the Foshan Municipal Government failed to provide evidence proving that Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch received and confirmed them, these two Comfort Letters do not constitute valid evidence and are not adopted by the court of first instance.

In summary, the claim of Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch is well-founded and should be supported. In accordance with Article 61, paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 138 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 6 and 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment:

The Foshan Municipal Government shall, within ten days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, bear compensatory liability for one-half of the portion of the principal debt of HKD 87,307,322.21 and interest (calculated according to the provisions of Credit Facility Agreements LC-1998-0929-COM-2473 and LC-1998-0931-COM-2473 from April 24, 2001 until full repayment) owed by Zhongya Company to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch, and the portion of the principal debt of HKD 78,293,395.48 and interest (calculated at the interest rate confirmed by Final Judgment No. 4924 of 2001 of the High Court of Hong Kong from October 20, 2001 until full repayment) owed by Jingshan Company to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch, that the debtors are unable to satisfy.

The Foshan Municipal Government, dissatisfied with the judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court. Its grounds of appeal are: 1. "A guarantee cannot be presumed" is a fundamental principle of guarantee law. "Will be responsible for resolving" does not mean an undertaking to repay the debt. Therefore, in terms of content, the Letters of Undertaking and Comfort Letters do not constitute a guarantee and are not legally binding. The appellee was also aware of this, and the appellant should not bear legal liability. 2. Assuming the Letters of Undertaking constitute a guarantee, they are guarantees for specific loans, not a maximum amount suretyship. The loans referred to in the Letters of Undertaking are unrelated to the claims sued upon by the appellee, and the appellant has no obligation to bear legal liability for the claims sued upon. 3. Assuming the Letters of Undertaking constitute a guarantee, it is an invalid guarantee, and the fault lies entirely with the appellee, so the appellant should not bear civil liability. 4. Assuming the Letters of Undertaking constitute a guarantee, the limitation period for the appellee to seek compensation from the appellant on that basis has expired. 5. The evidence submitted by the appellee is not in the proper legal form and is therefore not admissible as evidence under law. Therefore, the appellant requests that the judgment of first instance be reversed, all claims of the appellee be dismissed, and the appellee bear the litigation costs of this case.

Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch argued in its defense: 1. In terms of content, "not letting Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch suffer economic loss" is the core of the undertaking, therefore the Letters of Undertaking constitute a guarantee. 2. The loans referred to in the Letters of Undertaking are closely related to the loans in dispute in this case. 3. The primary responsibility for the invalidity of the Letters of Undertaking lies with the appellant. 4. The limitation period in this case has not expired. 5. The evidence submitted by the appellee is in the proper legal form.

Upon retrial during the second instance, this Court finds: The Letters of Undertaking Fo Fu Han (1994) No. 030, Fo Fu Han (1996) No. 144, and Fo Fu Han (1996) No. 146 issued by the Foshan Municipal Government to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch on May 8, 1994, October 24, 1996, and October 30, 1996 respectively; the letters of credit issued by Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch to Zhongya Company on October 25, 1996 and December 11, 1998; the letters of credit issued by Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch to Jingshan Company on October 29, 1996 and December 11, 1998; the minutes of the meetings held between the Foshan Municipal Government and Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch on February 19, 1998, August 19, 1998, and November 12, 1998; and the approval document Fo Jing Mao Fa [1998] No. 42 issued by the Foshan Municipal Government on November 12, 1998, "Reply on Agreeing that Delta Development Co., Ltd. Pledge Part of Its Equity Interests in Baihua Plaza as Collateral," are all supported by corresponding evidence on file, and this Court confirms them.

This Court holds: This case is a Hong Kong-related guarantee contract dispute. The parties did not stipulate the law applicable to the settlement of the contract dispute. The domicile of the defendant, the place of conclusion of the guarantee contract, and the place of performance are all located in Mainland China. The court of first instance, in accordance with Article 145 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and the principle of the closest connection, correctly determined that the law of Mainland China should apply to this case. The parties also have no objection to the application of the law of Mainland China to resolve this dispute. Therefore, the law of Mainland China shall apply to this case.

The primary focus of dispute in this case is whether the Letters of Undertaking issued by the Foshan Municipal Government to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch constitute a guarantee as defined in China's Guarantee Law. In this case, the Foshan Municipal Government issued three Letters of Undertaking to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch, each containing the same statement: "This government undertakes to supervise the company stationed in Hong Kong to earnestly fulfill its repayment obligations and repay the principal and interest of your bank's loans on time. If the company defaults or delays repayment of the principal and interest of your bank's loans, this government will be responsible for resolving the matter and will not let your bank suffer economic loss." First, in terms of name, the Letters of Undertaking are not guarantee letters, and whether they can constitute a guarantee should be determined by their content. Second, in terms of the content of the Letters of Undertaking, "will be responsible for resolving" and "will not let your bank suffer economic loss" do not contain a clear expression of willingness to assume guarantee liability or repay on behalf of the debtor. Third, in the letters of credit issued by Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch to Zhongya Company and Jingshan Company, under the item "Collateral and Legal Documents", in addition to the Foshan Municipal Government's Letters of Undertaking, there were also real estate mortgages, guarantees, and pledges of certificates of deposit. Furthermore, the Letters of Undertaking were listed under the "Other" documents category, distinct from "Guarantees", in these letters of credit. This indicates that Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch knew that the Letters of Undertaking were not guarantee letters. Finally, to address the issue of loans owed by directly affiliated enterprises of Foshan City, including Zhongya Company and Jingshan Company, to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch, the Foshan Municipal Government and Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch held three symposiums and produced meeting minutes. From the records of these three minutes, Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch never requested the Foshan Municipal Government to assume guarantee liability or repay on behalf of Zhongya Company and Jingshan Company, nor did the Foshan Municipal Government express any intention to assume guarantee liability or repay on behalf of the enterprises. Instead, the solution discussed by both parties was for the government to carry out asset restructuring of the enterprises at an appropriate time to resolve the existing debts. The Foshan Municipal Government also, on November 12, 1998, by document Fo Jing Mao Fa [1998] No. 42, approved the enterprise restructuring plan agreed upon between the relevant Foshan enterprises and Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch to resolve the issue of loans owed by Zhongya Company, Jingshan Company, and other enterprises to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch. In summary, the Foshan Municipal Government, from the written documents it issued to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch to its actual actions, never expressed any intention to assume guarantee liability or repay on behalf of its subordinate enterprises. The Letters of Undertaking it issued to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch do not constitute a guarantee within the meaning of China's Guarantee Law. Therefore, Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch's claim that the Foshan Municipal Government should bear compensatory liability for the invalid guarantee based on the Letters of Undertaking lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it. The Foshan Municipal Government's appeal grounds that the Letters of Undertaking do not constitute a guarantee and that it should not bear legal liability should be supported. The Foshan Municipal Government shall not bear any legal liability to Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch. The other appeal grounds of the Foshan Municipal Government are all objections to the judgment of first instance under the assumption that the Letters of Undertaking constitute a guarantee. Since it is determined that the Letters of Undertaking do not constitute a guarantee, there is no need to examine those grounds. The judgment of the court of first instance erred in both fact-finding and application of law and should be reversed. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 6 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders the following judgment:

1. The Civil Judgment (2001) Yue Fa Jing Er Chu Zi No. 1 of the Guangdong High People's Court is reversed.

2. The claims of Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch are dismissed.

The court costs of the first instance, HKD 798,394, shall be borne by Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch; the court costs of the second instance, HKD 798,394, shall be borne by Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch. This amount has been prepaid to this Court by the Foshan Municipal People's Government. Bank of Communications Hong Kong Branch shall, within ten days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, directly pay this amount to the Foshan Municipal People's Government. This Court will not process a refund.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yun

Acting Judge: Chen Jizhong
